text: The Patriots' dominant 20-3 victory over the Steelers at Gillette Stadium in their Week 2 home opener showcased a defense that picked up the slack against Aaron Rodgers and company, with TreVeyon Henderson punching in a touchdown as New England cruised to the win—though the celebration was tempered by the discovery that starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle during the game. Despite the lopsided scoreline, the offense hasn't yet recaptured the rhythm that fueled last season's Super Bowl run, suggesting that even in convincing fashion, there's still work to be done on that side of the ball. The win was historic enough to mark another milestone: the Patriots became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins in franchise history, a testament to sustained excellence across decades. Head Coach Mike Vrabel and his players will be digesting the performance and managing injuries as they look ahead, with the immediate concern being how the loss of Onwenu impacts the offensive line going forward.
